question: Of the 29 families the first stale-builder sweep did not reach, which ones' committed artifacts still come from their own build scripts, and where they do not, what actually differs?
companionRecord: data/rcap-grade-a/fable-packet-factory/BUILD_REPRODUCIBILITY_STALE_SCREEN_2026-09-09.json covers the first 25; this record covers the 29 the same screen missed. Together they are 54 of the 54 families the corrected screen matches

changesNothing.note: This lane measures. Every rebuild was restored from git and verified byte-identical before the next family; the tool reported every family restored and zero host bleed, and the four hand rebuilds were restored and checked the same way. data/rcap-grade-a/fable-packet-factory/BUILD_REPRODUCIBILITY.json still holds its original 87 rows - this sweep was pointed at a different path precisely so it could not overwrite them

screenVerification.what: every one of these 29 satisfies the stated criterion independently checked here: the owning build script has a commit strictly newer than the delivered fixtures/canonical.pdf

method.step1: scripts/grade-a-packet-factory-24h/measure-build-reproducibility.mjs run ONCE over all 29 families via a new --families flag, writing to a new record via a new --out flag, so the 87-row corpus record was never rewritten and no run replaced a previous run's rows
method.step2: --timeout 2400000 (40 minutes per family), long enough for every custom-pleading raster stage in this set; nothing was recorded UNBUILDABLE for a timeout
method.step3: divergence read at appearance level, not from digests: pdftotext and pdftotext -layout of committed against rebuilt fixtures, byte-offset comparison with cmp -l, date-normalised re-comparison, field-by-field comparison of reports/actual-writes.json, and for West Virginia a 100dpi pixel-by-pixel raster comparison of every page
method.step4: four families were rebuilt again by hand into scratch space so their rebuilt bytes could be examined after the sweep had restored the tree: co_pardoned_conviction_seal-set, pa_age70_deceased-set, sd_arrest_expungement-set and wv_conv_multiple_misdemeanors-set
method.step5: packet PDFs are reported separately from the raster stage and from recorded source hashes, because a delivered directory that never ran its raster stage reads as DIVERGES against a rebuild that does, and that is not a packet-byte divergence

headlines: 25 of these 29 reproduce their delivered packet PDFs byte for byte. Four do not: two by a date stamp alone, one substantively, and one that cannot be measured because its builder refuses to finish.

20 of the 22 COMPLETE_PACKET_PROVEN families in this set reproduce their packet bytes exactly. The two that do not are co_pardoned_conviction_seal-set, whose entire divergence is a wall-clock stamp, and wv_conv_multiple_misdemeanors-set, which could not be measured.

The wall-clock category the first sweep found empty is not empty here: co_pardoned_conviction_seal-set and pa_age70_deceased-set each differ from their rebuild in 14 and 16 bytes, every one inside /ModDate and /CreationDate. Both builders now write a fixed D:20260829000000Z, so the stale bytes are the delivered ones, and the defect is already repaired in the script.

wv_conv_multiple_misdemeanors-set is the finding a repair lane should take first. It is COMPLETE_PACKET_PROVEN, its official source has not moved, and its own builder exits 1 on 26 blocking selection-control findings while producing a canonical fixture that is visibly poorer than the delivered one across three of four pages.

sd_arrest_expungement-set is the only substantive packet divergence, and the packet PDF part of it is inert: one empty appearance stream's /Matrix. What actually moved is its field classification (107 required-before-filing fields down to 28) and its product wiring, which the rebuild strips of its entire binding block.

Seven families pin an in-repo source that has since moved. Six of them pin data/record-clearing/legal-design-packet-set-manifests.json; the seventh, ut_pet_acquittal-set, cites a stale compiled-profile hash in the participant-facing instructions themselves. No packet byte changes in any of the seven.

toolRepairsMade.why: the first lane recorded five limitations in this tool. Three of them are structural rather than per-family, and are repaired here rather than worked around
repairs: --out <path>: the report path is now selectable. The tool rewrites its whole record on every run, so a partial sweep aimed at the default path silently replaces a completed sweep's rows - which had already happened once in this repository. This sweep wrote to its own record and the 87-row corpus record was never opened for writing.

--families <json>: a JSON array of family ids restricts the sweep, so a named subset is covered by ONE run instead of a loop of runs that each replace the last. denominator.notSwept and complete are now computed against what the run was asked to sweep rather than against the whole corpus.

determineInvocation now recognises a builder with no process.argv[1] guard whose top-level dispatch falls through to its own family id, instead of filing it UNKNOWN_INVOCATION. That misclassification cost the first sweep a true positive (il-seal-edu-set). The branch was verified against build-census-v1-sd_arrest_expungement-set.mjs, the one builder in this set with that shape.

every row now carries builderRewroteOwnDirectory, so a REPRODUCES that only proves the script exited cleanly can be told from one where the builder actually authored the bytes. All 28 buildable families in this set rewrote their own directory.
notRepaired: a builder that asserts a required flag still reads as UNBUILDABLE; no family in this set does that, so the fix could not be verified here and was left alone.

the invocationBasis string can still claim a 'direct-invocation guard' for a builder that has none - see sd_arrest_expungement-set's row. The invocation it picks is correct; only the explanation is wrong.
the 600s default timeout is unchanged; this sweep passed --timeout 2400000 instead.
toolRepairsMade.didTheTopLevelEntryFixChangeAnyOutcomeHe: no. It fired for no family in this set. sd_arrest_expungement-set, the only builder with that shape, was already reaching the right invocation through an unrelated const-name coincidence. The repair is still correct and still needed for the next sweep.

sourceHashDrift.consequence: six of the seven source-hash-drift families pin a repository file that has moved since they were built. This is in-repo staleness, not a custody-mount difference: the drifting file is committed here. It changes no packet byte in any of the six
sourceHashDrift.identityRefresh: five of them (in, ky_criminal, ri_marijuana, vt_exp_deferred, vt_seal_under_25) carry a 639-byte identityRefresh block recording an earlier move of the same file on 2026-09-05, with anchorsCompared 1 / anchorsIdentical 1. The builder writes that block only for the pin it knew about, so a rebuild today drops it

the family's own builder cannot complete today. Entered as `node scripts/build-census-v1-wv_conv_multiple_misdemeanors-set.mjs` it exits 1 from its shared host's byte gate with 26 blocking findings, all one check - selection_control_carries_artifact_derived_text_or_vector_mark - covering 13 selection controls on SCA-C906 across both fixtures (SingleFelonyCB, MultipleFelonyCB, SingleSatisfiedCB, MultilpleSatisfiedCB, ExpungementCB1/2, PriorOrderCB1/2, CurrentOrderCB1/2, FirstClassMailCB, HandDeliveryCB, CertifiedMailCB). The delivered build-findings.json records blocking: [] and findingCount: 0

evidence.notASourceDrift: the official form is identical: both the delivered and the rebuilt source-receipt bind SCA-C906 at 43b5606c9faf6fcf4d6f73c1d97cf1bd87798158dee1b6f3381c8a0472b4b64c, 176072 bytes, exactHashVerified true
evidence.whatTheRebuiltBytesLookLike: the failed rebuild still wrote fixtures. Its canonical.pdf is 199874 bytes against the delivered 173531. Rastered at 100dpi and compared pixel by pixel, pages 1-3 hold ink the rebuild does not reproduce: 7013 px on page 1, 7516 px on page 2 and 662 px on page 3 are inked only in the delivered fixture, against 409 px inked only in the rebuild (page 1) and page 4 identical. Today's builder produces a visibly poorer packet and then its own gate refuses it
evidence.whatThisDoesNotEstablish: nothing here shows the delivered bytes are wrong. It shows they cannot be reproduced, and that the family sits at COMPLETE_PACKET_PROVEN behind a builder that no longer produces them. Settling the delivered bytes is a repair lane's and an independent reader's work, not this lane's

diverges substantively, and in both directions. Packet PDFs: 51 bytes larger, and the only PDF change is one empty text-widget appearance stream whose /Matrix goes from the identity [1 0 0 1 0 0] to [0.9999999999999999 0 0 1.1909259259259246 0 0]; the stream body is '/Tx BMC EMC', so it paints nothing - pdftotext -layout output is identical and reports/actual-writes.json records identical drawn values. The real divergence is in the sidecars. production-field-map.json: requiredBeforeFilingCount 107 -> 28, with 81 fields (Case Number, COUNTY Name, Date of Birth defendant, Cell phone - plaintiff and 77 more) dropped from required-before-filing and buildPolicyCategory keys (type_guard, government_identifier, mapping_conflict) added that the delivered map does not have at all. product-wiring.json: the rebuild is POORER, 97 lines -> 17, dropping the entire 17-key binding block including paymentEligible, sponsorshipEligible, whyPaymentIsClosed, lastIndependentVerification and the three-stage binding.routeKeys list. Rebuilding this family as delivered would delete its route binding record

evidence.aClaimTheDeliveredBytesDoNotSupport: the delivered build-findings.json states '107 field(s) the filing needs are classified required-before-filing and surfaced in participant-instructions.md rather than guessed.' participant-instructions.md is byte-identical in the delivered and rebuilt directories, and its 'Required before filing or service' section lists 9 items - Judicial Circuit number, State's Attorney name and mailing address, notice recipient name and mailing address, the dismissal proof, and three checks. Neither 107 nor the rebuild's 28 matches the document being cited, but 107 is the delivered figure and it is the further from it
evidence.direction: MIXED: the field map gets richer, the product wiring gets poorer

families.invocationBasisRecordedBySweep: the sweep stored 'direct-invocation guard enters this family id with no argument'. That string is wrong: this builder has no process.argv[1] guard at all. determineInvocation reached the right answer by coincidence - the file contains `const target = "sd_arrest_expungement-set"` inside its --instruction-repair-only branch, and that const resolved the `runFamilyById(target, [])` call. The invocation itself is correct and was confirmed empirically (the builder rewrote its own directory)
